parts.text: Every day, Robyn dispatches sixteen emails.
Out of these, seven are related to her job, and two-thirds of the remaining ones are sent to her family members.
One-third of the other emails are directed to her boyfriend.
Can you determine the number of emails she sends to her boyfriend each day?

assumptions: “The other emails” refers to the same non-job remainder partitioned between family and boyfriend emails.

items.question: Every day, Robyn dispatches sixteen emails. Out of these, seven are related to her job, and two-thirds of the remaining ones are sent to her family members. One-third of the other emails are directed to her boyfriend. Can you determine the number of emails she sends to her boyfriend each day?

validator_context.gold_reasoning:
Robyn sends 16 - 7 = <<16-7=9>>9 non-work emails.
She sends 9 * 2 / 3 = <<9*2/3=6>>6 emails to family.
There are 9 - 6 = <<9-6=3>>3 emails remaining.
Of the remaining 3, 1/3 are to her boyfriend, so Robyn sends him 3 * 1 / 3 = <<3*1/3=1>>1 email a day.

parts.text: Billy is peeling and cutting potatoes in preparation for making potato salad for his big family reunion barbecue.
It's a big event, so he has 60 potatoes to get through.
The potatoes are roughly the same size, so it takes about the same amount of time to peel and cut each one.
It takes Billy about a minute and a half to peel a potato, but only about 5.5 seconds to cut it up.
How long will it take Billy to finish prepping the potatoes?

semantic_notes: Contextual setup introduces no quantitative state.
This clause establishes that the following per-potato durations apply uniformly to all potatoes.

assumptions: One minute is converted to 60 seconds, and the per-potato durations apply to all 60 potatoes.

validator_context.gold_reasoning:
There are 60 potatoes, and Billy takes a minute and a half to peel each one, or 60 potatoes * 1.5 minutes per potato = <<60*1.5=90>>90 minutes.
Billy only takes 5.5 seconds to cut the potatoes, so it takes 5.5 seconds * 60 potatoes=330 seconds= 5.5 minutes to cut the potatoes.
So it will take him a total of 90 minutes peeling + 5.5 minutes cutting = <<90+5.5=95.5>>95.5 minutes total prepping the potatoes.

parts.text: Mrs. Tatiana owns a bustling grocery store that sells a variety of fruits and vegetables, including carrots and apples.
The price of apples remains constant, but the price of carrots in the grocery store increases by 5% of the original price every year.
If the price of apples is $100, which doesn't change, what would be the price of carrots after three years if it was $120 initially?
(Round to the nearest integer)

semantic_notes: This clause introduces the store and products but no quantitative arithmetic state.
Because the annual carrot increase is explicitly based on the original price, it is a fixed additive increase rather than a compounded percentage increase.

assumptions: The active operator registry has no rounding operator with which to encode rounding to the nearest integer.
